The FDE workshop01 / 30
Start with people

You are an FDE.

Your job is to connect with stakeholders and get to a working solution.

Connect

Who does the work? Where do they struggle?

→

Understand

What business result would make this worthwhile?

→

Deliver

Build it, verify it, and help people use it.

What value will this create for the people who use it?
The FDE workshop02 / 30
Learning outcomes

What you’ll
take away.

1

Deploy a basic service

Connect a frontend, backend, and database.

2

Use tests for confidence

Understand how tests provide evidence that things work.

3

4

5

The FDE workshop06 / 30
Desk / Feature to implement

The next feature: Assign to me.

Claim from ticket details

Show Unassigned. Agents can claim; disable the button while saving. Customers can only view.

Save one owner

Use the signed-in agent. Save the assignee in PostgreSQL and keep it visible after refresh.

Handle competing claims

Only one agent can win. Show a useful conflict message and let the other agent refresh.

Session

Login stores an HttpOnly session cookie. Anonymous ticket reads return 401.

Ticket reads

GET /api/tickets lists tickets. GET /api/tickets/1 returns details.

New contract

Suggested: POST /api/tickets/:id/assign. Derive the agent from the session.

The FDE workshop17 / 30
Git / Branch

Work on a feature in its own branch.

Keep main stable while you build the feature.

1 / 4

git switch -c feature/claim-ticket
git push -u origin feature/claim-ticket

A branch points to a commit. New commits on it leave main unchanged.

The FDE workshop18 / 30
Git / Merge

Bring the feature branch into main.

Review the feature, then merge it into main.

0 / 5

git switch main
git merge --no-ff feature/claim-ticket

Merge commit M has two parents, one from each branch.

The FDE workshop19 / 30
Git / Pull

Update your local main branch.

Pull downloads missing commits, then fast-forwards your local branch.

0 / 4

git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main

Local main now includes the remote commits. No merge commit was needed.

The FDE workshop21 / 30
Kata acceptance criteria

One ticket.
Exactly one assignee.

Successful claim

An agent claims an unassigned ticket. Refresh and a second agent see the assignee.

Server identity

Use the logged-in session. Customers cannot claim, including through the API.

Concurrent claims

Exactly one succeeds. Return 409 to the other agent and preserve the winner.

Failure recovery

Missing or failed requests leave data unchanged and show useful feedback.

Evidence

Prove persistence, permissions, conflicts, and both browser outcomes.

Review

Keep baseline tests passing and 100% source coverage. Explain the assertions.

The FDE workshop23 / 30
Security demonstration

Can Amina read
Bilal’s ticket?

After the team demos

Amina signs in.
Ticket 2 belongs to Bilal.

Open “Update our billing contact.” Repeat with GET /api/tickets/2 using Amina’s session.

Reproduce

Login works. Customer ownership checks are missing.

Fix

Scope both reads: agents see all, customers see their own.

Prove

Amina gets 404 for ticket 2. Sara retains access.

100% source coverage can still miss a business rule.
The FDE workshop24 / 30
Security checklist

Review the risks.
Ask for evidence.

Access

Check identity, object-level permissions, and privileged actions.

Inputs and limits

Validate input, protect database queries, and limit abuse.

Configuration

Protect secrets. Check exposed endpoints and dependencies.

Security references

OWASP API Security
Top 10
2023 edition

Use Cloudflare’s security-audit skill to review the training app.

The FDE workshop25 / 30
Codebase health

Quick fixes add up.
Make changes safer.

When rules are duplicated

Same rule in several places

The interface and backend can give different answers.

One file does too much

A small change affects unrelated behavior.

Tests miss user outcomes

Refactors break tests, or bugs reach the user.

After a small refactor

One place for each rule

The backend applies the same policy everywhere.

Clear module responsibilities

Each part owns a specific decision.

Tests check behavior

The same user outcomes hold after the change.

The FDE workshop26 / 30
Maintain the codebase

Make the next change
easier to review.

Inspect the code

Look for repeated rules, vague names, and modules that do too much.

Pick one improvement

Ask improve-codebase-design to suggest a change. Review its reasoning.

Change one thing

Preserve behavior, run relevant checks, and review the diff.

Review the suggestion. You decide what to change.

The FDE workshop28 / 30
UI judgment

A polished screen
can still be hard to use.

Watch someone use it

Can they find the main action and tell what happened?

Check every state

Review loading, empty, error, success, and narrow screens.

Fix what gets in the way

Improve readability, hierarchy, contrast, and spacing.

Ask during review

What should I do next?
Did it work?
How do I fix a problem?

Use these questions during review. Check the changes in a browser.
